decisions.reason: F1 incorrectly said finite residue fields; on P1 over C the residue field at every closed point is C. The actual suppliers assert finite extensions of k. This is a nonfatal wording defect: steps 5.1 and 6.1 use extension degrees and the tower law, never finite cardinalities. Replaced the phrase with residue fields finite over k.

The fixed-trace definition, published smooth-projective duality and normalization lemmas, principal-parts presentation and residue-descent theorem explicitly assume AC. The unqualified opening of the Remark did not establish that prerequisite; putting def-axiom-of-choice in deps alone does not license those implications. Added an explicit inherited AC assumption covering the entire remark.

The title omitted the rational-point condition that the Statement and Given already impose. A smooth genus-one real curve with no real points cannot be a real plane cubic: a homogeneous real cubic is odd on the connected sphere and therefore has a zero. The real double cover y^2=-(x^4+1) has no real points in either its x-chart or its infinity chart v^2=-(1+u^4). The four simple geometric branch points give genus one. This refutes the unqualified title, not the existing conditional theorem. Qualified the title by with a rational point; the Statement and proof are unchanged.

reviews.reason: Checked flatness at closed stalks using torsion-free modules over a PID and at the generic stalk over k(D); the proof does not assert finite generation of individual stalks. Local Cartier equations give coefficients e_p, the supplied weighted fibre sum and tower law give the degree formula, and Cartier/Weil plus degree-zero principal divisors make the line-bundle degree well-defined. Only F1 wording changed; the Statement is byte-for-byte unchanged. Focused precheck and rendercheck both exited 0.

Under the now explicit AC hypothesis, the curve duality supplier applies to the smooth proper geometrically integral curve and gives projectivity and a one-dimensional H1(omega). Its complete comparison proof 1.3–1.5, 2.2 and 3.1 uses the raw +du Cartier cocycle and the normalized -du trace-one point class, with the one-point sheaf-Ext edge making the equality global. Separable residue-field splitting and trace base change give the negative trace sum; multiplication of Cartier-twist sequences gives the general pairing. The final residue-degree caveat is correct even when Tr(1)=0. No Statement or Definition section exists or changed. Rendercheck and the scoped strict contract check pass; precheck is not applicable to this remark.

For g=1, RR gives h0(L)=3 and the degree threshold 3=2g+1 gives a closed immersion with pullback O(1)=L. The saturated image ideal is prime because its quotient embeds in the section ring of an integral curve; the standard graded Laurent chart has fraction-field transcendence degree 2, so the ideal has height one and a homogeneous irreducible generator F. Weighted Bezout with a nonvanishing linear section equates deg F with the divisor degree 3, including nonrational intersection points. RR on a signed degree-one divisor supplies an effective equivalent divisor of degree one and thus a rational point. All supplier hypotheses, including AC, are met. Only the title changed; no Statement or Definition changed. Precheck, rendercheck and the scoped strict contract check passed.
